claim.text: Symbolized first-Rust-frame DHAT groups Term::clone and engine::solve account for >=95% of net extra bytes, Term::clone >=90% of net extra blocks, and six libc heap functions >=65% of extra Callgrind Ir for a failed-first-head two-clause R128 comparison.
claim.scope: Two Valgrind 3.22.0 ELF64 artifacts of identical synthetic Gen18 vs retired Gen19 workloads; first run exploratory, second same-workload held-out execution.
assumptions: DHAT v2 allocation site tables and human Total log refer to the same process
Callgrind Ir entries are fully captured by exclusive function cost rows
Symbolized first project Rust frame is a heuristic grouping, not a unique source line
The held-out run uses an identical compiler and synthetic workloads
forbidden_promotions: No independent experimental authorship or independent semantic oracle
No hardware cycles or native walltime attributed to named symbols
No generalization to unseen Prolog programs
Do not reinterpret the exploratory run as prospectively preregistered

specification.intended_object: Read-only mapping of two immutable raw Valgrind artifacts into typed, signed per-group heap and instruction deltas.
invariants: Every DHAT site's bytes and blocks sum to independent log Total
Every Callgrind function-exclusive Ir sum equals reported summary
Preserve signed differences and unknown symbol groups
Controls within frozen 0.9 to 1.1 ratio interval
known_answer_cases: T2 first-success, T3, T1 and builtin controls

implementation.environment: Python 3 standard library interpreting immutable Valgrind 3.22.0 ELF64 DHAT v2 JSON/log and Callgrind text; no runtime engine edits.
implementation.live_entrypoint: Offline `inspect(archive, heldout=True)` -> `parse_dhat`, `parse_callgrind`, signed grouped deltas and frozen gates.
implementation.representation: Typed mapping of original bytes, blocks, simulated instruction references, program/process archive hashes and signed group deltas.

metric.name: Signed DHAT group delta bytes/blocks and exclusive Callgrind Ir contribution share
metric.units: DHAT whole-process allocated bytes, heap blocks, Callgrind simulator-counted instruction references
equivalence_attacks: Replace first successful same-signature head by failing head
Compare T2 first success with same predicate cardinality
T1/T3/builtin controls under the unchanged ownership branch
Different process IDs and PC addresses normalized by symbol label

black_box: Six fixed matching primary/control cases in original and held-out artifacts
Inherited Generation21 264 strict CLI cases per ABI, not rerun here
structural: DHAT per-site allocation count reconciliation to human tool Total
Callgrind exclusive cost reconciliation to summary
SHA256 provenance of both original artifact ZIPs
Exact frozen symbol-list and ratio thresholds
property_based: Not applicable: only immutable historical profiler dumps were available
metamorphic: Differing raw address mapping with same symbolic identity
fuzzing: Not applicable: parser synthetic known-answer and malformed-input tests instead
historical: Generation21 native timing 9.99× ELF64 / 8.94× i686 and Valgrind aggregate ratios
Generation20 traced GlobalAlloc and continuation-copy predictions

matched_baselines: Pinned Gen18 and Gen19 same-workload symbolized Valgrind profiles on ELF64
Same normalizer for both versions and both runs
negative_controls: T1 R128 and builtin true/0 R128
Malformed DHAT log and Callgrind summary unit negatives
controls.compute_parity: The experiment reinterprets immutable raw traces; both versions previously compiled and measured on same runner target; no new profiling resources.
controls.parameter_parity: The two artifacts reuse the identical fixed query, clause order, repeat counts and solution limits per case.
controls.sampling_parity: One process per profiler tool/mode/version/case in each of the two runs; a same-workload repeat, not new statistical population.
controls.data_access_parity: Original and held-out archive IDs and SHA256 fixed before normalized source-symbol analysis promotion.

preregistration.prediction: After exploratory run, frozen before held-out inspection: T2 first-fail R128 >=95% net extra DHAT bytes from Term::clone+engine::solve; >=90% net blocks from Term::clone; >=65% net extra Ir from six fixed libc names; all four unchanged-path controls 0.9 to 1.1.
preregistration.primary_metric: Typed region of signed source-symbol DHAT and Callgrind attribution shares with exact raw-sum and negative-control gates.
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Same-workload held-out instrument run; no independent workload, bootstrap confidence interval or independent author. All signed groups retained.
preregistration.kill_condition: Any missing source artifact or frame, failed DHAT/log or Callgrind summary reconciliation, unexpected control ratio, unstable label mapping, or held-out threshold miss.
preregistration.stop_condition: Do not reclassify signs or tune grouping/thresholds after held-out run; do not introduce a new solver optimization.
preregistration.promotion_rule: M only for narrowly reproducible symbol-grouped process-wide metrics; native CPU causality and external generalization stay H.

result.observed: Held-out run reproduces +897128 DHAT bytes and +24384 DHAT blocks; net extra bytes attributed to Term::clone +447040 and engine::solve +450088; all extra blocks to Term::clone; six libc names +8579808 / +11619544 Callgrind Ir. All unchanged-path controls passed.
result.effect_size: Typed attribution-share tuple: 100% of net DHAT allocated bytes in two Rust symbolized sites; 100% of net DHAT blocks in Term::clone; 73.8394553177% of net Callgrind Ir in six heap-management functions.
result.uncertainty: Symbol names/stack truncation and inlining shape the attribution; identical workloads and independent profiling software but no independently authored study or ISO semantic witness. No hardware-cycle attribution.
